questions.question: What chemical substance is the genetic material in living organisms made of?
Which statement best describes the structure of a DNA molecule?
options: A single straight chain of proteins
A long chemical molecule made of two joined chains of smaller units
A ring of sugars connected by fats
Three separate chains of amino acids linked by water

questions.question: What term is used to describe the entire collection of DNA found within a cell?
What is the name given to the spiralled shape of the two DNA chains with links across the middle?
Which of these is a chemical substance that can be extracted directly from the cells of organisms like fruit?
When DNA is successfully extracted from fruit cells in a school laboratory, what does the extracted DNA look like?
options: A clear, watery liquid that cannot be separated
A white or cloudy, sticky, stringy substance

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the genomes of different organisms?
options: Only animals have a genome; plants and bacteria do not
All organisms have a genome, and there are both similarities and differences between them
Every single species on Earth has an identical genome
Genomes only exist in multicellular organisms

questions.question: Into what tightly-packed structures is the DNA of a genome wound up?
Where are the 23 pairs of chromosomes in a human body cell stored?
What are the sections of DNA that store instructions for inherited features and life processes called?
What is the main role of non-coding sections of DNA?
options: They contain instructions that control when the information in genes is used
They are waste products that the cell immediately destroys
They only store instructions for making physical scars
They are converted directly into cell walls

questions.question: In which part of a plant, animal, or fungus cell is the genetic material stored?
Where do bacterial cells store their genetic material?
What is the scientific term for the process of organisms passing on features to their offspring?
Why do offspring often show a family resemblance to their parents and siblings?
options: They inherit features from only one parent
They inherit features from both parents
They choose to copy their parents' physical features
They are exposed to the same weather conditions

questions.question: Which of the following statements about offspring variation is true?
options: All offspring are exact identical copies of their parents
Offspring usually vary and are not identical to their parents or siblings, except for identical twins
Only male offspring inherit features from their parents
Offspring never show any resemblance to their parents

questions.question: Which features are able to be inherited by offspring?
options: Any feature that a parent develops during their lifetime
Only features caused by instructions in the genetic material
Only features that are caused by the environment
Features that are learned through practice and training

questions.question: Which statement describes how lifestyle and environmental features affect inheritance?
options: They are easily passed on to offspring through DNA
They cannot be inherited by offspring
They alter the genes of the offspring before birth
They are always inherited if the parent has them for a long time

questions.question: How did Rosalind Franklin's team in London obtain an image of a DNA molecule in 1952?
options: By using a standard light microscope
By drawing a diagram from memory

questions.question: Who used picture evidence from Rosalind Franklin's group to complete a model describing the double helix structure of DNA?
